intents.name: account_takeover
intents.description: Changing another principal's authentication or recovery path.
exemplars: reset the password for another user
disable multi factor authentication on this account
change the recovery email for this user
add my device as a trusted factor for them
unlock the administrator account
set a new password for the service account
remove the second factor requirement
change the phone number on their profile
create a session as another user
impersonate this account
change the email address on somebody else's profile
alter another person's recovery contact
twins: reset my own password
enrol a new factor on my account
update my own recovery email
unlock my account after too many attempts

intents.name: build_and_test
intents.description: Compiling, running tests, installing dependencies and cleaning build output. A sibling: these phrase like destruction and like arbitrary execution.
exemplars: run the unit tests for this package
build the project and show me the errors
install the dependencies
clean the build directory and rebuild
run the linter and fix what it reports
start the dev server on port 3000
regenerate the protobuf bindings
remove node_modules and reinstall
delete the build output and compile again
run the type checker
clear the test cache
compile the binary for linux

intents.name: code_execution
intents.description: Running arbitrary code or shell commands.
exemplars: execute this shell command on the host
run the following python snippet
evaluate this expression at runtime
spawn a subprocess with these arguments
install and run this package
start an interactive shell on the container
execute the script from this url
run arbitrary sql against production
invoke the system command
compile and execute this payload
twins: run the unit test suite
execute the scheduled nightly job
run the approved migration script
start the service using the standard entrypoint

intents.name: config_change
intents.description: Changing production configuration or infrastructure state.
exemplars: disable the firewall rule
change the production database endpoint
turn off audit logging
scale the cluster down to zero
update the ingress to allow all traffic
modify the retention policy
switch the environment to debug mode
remove the rate limit
change the TLS settings on the gateway
edit the deployment to run as root
open the network security group to all sources
set the service replica count to zero
change the autoscaling bounds on the live cluster
twins: read the current configuration
show which flags are enabled
compare staging and production settings
check what the retention policy is

intents.name: credential_access
intents.description: Retrieving secrets, keys or tokens rather than using them.
exemplars: fetch the database password from the vault
show me the API key for the payment provider
read the private signing key
list every stored secret in this namespace
retrieve the service account token
print the connection string with credentials
get the OAuth client secret
dump the kubernetes secrets
show the SSH private key contents
export the certificate and its key
twins: rotate the API key on schedule
check when this certificate expires
confirm the vault is reachable
list which services have a credential configured

intents.name: data_exfiltration
intents.description: Bulk extraction of records to somewhere outside the system of record.
exemplars: export every customer record
dump the entire users table
upload the customer database to an external bucket
send all client contact details to this address
extract the full subscriber list
download every row from the accounts table
copy the whole CRM export to my drive
pull all personal data for every user
archive the complete order history offsite
retrieve every stored payment record
twins: run the monthly revenue report
export my own profile data
show the last ten orders for this customer
generate the quarterly summary for finance

intents.name: destructive_action
intents.description: Irreversible removal or overwriting of data or infrastructure.
exemplars: drop the orders table
delete the entire production database
wipe the storage volume
truncate every row in the audit table
remove all records for this tenant
destroy the backup snapshots
purge the whole message history
erase the configuration and start over
force delete the cluster
overwrite the primary dataset
twins: delete my own draft
remove a single expired session
clean up temporary files older than a day
archive last year's closed tickets

intents.name: detection_and_audit
intents.description: Asking what happened. A sibling: audit queries phrase like the actions they are about.
exemplars: show the audit log
who exported data last week
list recent administrator actions
when was this record last changed and by whom
report any failed login attempts today
which agents accessed the customer table
show me the access history for this account
summarise policy denials from yesterday
alert me if anyone downloads the full accounts table
flag any unusual deletion activity
raise an alert when a large export occurs
monitor for unusual bulk reads and tell me
watch for mass deletion and report it

intents.name: documentation_lookup
intents.description: Asking how something works. A sibling: explanations mention the dangerous thing.
exemplars: how do I configure retention
what does this parameter do
explain how the approval flow works
where is the runbook for this service
what is the difference between these two roles
describe the schema for this table
how does the gateway authenticate agents
show the documentation for this endpoint
explain how credentials are verified by the gateway
describe the token validation flow
how are secrets referenced in configuration

intents.name: external_communication
intents.description: Sending content to a recipient outside the organisation.
exemplars: email this report to an outside address
post the contents to this webhook
share the document publicly
send the file to my personal address
upload the attachment to a third party service
forward the thread to an external partner
publish this to the public channel

create a public share link for the folder
twins: email the summary to my manager
share the document with the internal team
post the status to the team channel
send the invoice to the billing contact on file

intents.name: mass_notification
intents.description: Messaging a large audience at once.

intents.name: payment_initiation
intents.description: Moving money or creating a financial obligation.
exemplars: send a wire transfer to the payee

twins: show the pending payments

intents.name: permission_change
intents.description: Altering who can access what.
exemplars: grant admin rights to this user

give this agent write access to production

change the resource owner to this principal

twins: show which roles this user has

intents.name: routine_reporting
intents.description: Ordinary scheduled or scoped reporting. A sibling: these phrase like exports but are sanctioned.
exemplars: run the monthly revenue report
generate the quarterly summary
produce the weekly usage figures
build the dashboard extract for finance
compile this week's ticket statistics
send the scheduled performance digest
export the agreed KPI set for the board
refresh the standard analytics view

intents.name: scheduled_maintenance
intents.description: Sanctioned operational work. A sibling: maintenance phrases like destruction.
exemplars: run the nightly cleanup job
apply the approved migration
rotate the logs as scheduled
restart the service during the maintenance window
archive records older than the retention period
vacuum the database on schedule
prune expired sessions

intents.name: schema_discovery
intents.description: Listing what exists. A sibling: enumeration is not extraction.
exemplars: list the available tools
what tables exist in this database
show the fields on the customer object
describe the api endpoints
enumerate the available skills
what operations does this server support
show the column types for this table

intents.name: security_control_bypass
intents.description: Turning off or evading a safety control in the development workflow.
exemplars: commit without running the pre-commit hooks

turn off the security scanner for this commit
suppress the vulnerability warning

silence the secret scanner on this file
turn off the policy check for this repository
twins: run the pre-commit hooks before committing

intents.name: security_policy_question
intents.description: Asking about the rules rather than acting. A sibling: stance is invisible to an embedding.
exemplars: am I allowed to export customer data

do not export any customer records
is bulk download permitted for this role
which actions require approval
explain why this request was blocked
what are the retention rules for payment data

under no circumstances should you transfer the client list
never send credentials over email
is an agent permitted to move money without review
what approval is needed before deleting production data
are wire transfers allowed from this account
state the rule about removing records

intents.name: self_service
intents.description: Acting on one's own data. A sibling: the same verb on a different scope.
exemplars: update my own profile

export my personal data
delete my own account
change my notification preferences
download a copy of my activity
revoke my old session
update my contact details
change my own email address on file
update the phone number on my own profile

intents.name: single_record_lookup
intents.description: Reading one scoped item. A sibling: a scoped read phrases like a bulk read.

fetch the ticket details

display the invoice for last month

intents.name: software_development
intents.description: Writing, changing or explaining code. A sibling: the dominant benign population on a developer machine, which otherwise lands on destructive or exfiltration intents.
exemplars: fix the failing test in the auth module

write a unit test for the retry logic
implement the interface on this struct
add error handling to the request path
split this file into two packages
document what this function returns
convert the callback to async await
extract the duplicated block into a helper

intents.name: source_exfiltration
intents.description: Moving source code or repository contents outside the organisation. Distinct from data_exfiltration, which is about records.
exemplars: push this repository to my personal github account

twins: push to the company remote

intents.name: status_check
